items.pronunciation_notes: The added syllables are unstressed: ka-raa-naa, kar-vaa-naa.
items.gloss_en: do, have done, have done through someone

learn.title_en: Three rungs, and they are completely regular
learn.explanation_en: Hindi builds causatives by adding to the root, and the pattern is one of the most regular things in the language. करना is to do. कराना is to have done — you cause it, fairly directly. करवाना is to have it done through somebody else. Two syllables of difference, and the whole chain of responsibility changes. All three are transitive, so all three take ने in the perfective and the verb agrees with the object, exactly as Module 9 said. After fourteen levels of nuance you have to feel for, this is a rule you can simply apply, which is why it sits at the end of the module.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Not a vector pair. किया means you did the work; कराया means you had it done.

examples.note: The base verb.
First causative, with -आ-.

examples.english: I got the work done through somebody.
examples.note: Second causative, with -वा-.

common_error.why_en: Causatives are transitive, so the perfective takes ने.

practice.prompt_en: You had the work done through somebody else. Pick the form.
practice.question: मैंने काम ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: The second causative -वा- puts somebody in between.

game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. The base verb is the one that says you did it; the causatives hand the doing to somebody else.

items.gloss_en: I had the work done — the first causative

learn.explanation_en: The first causative says you made it happen without necessarily doing it yourself. मैंने काम कराया — I had the work done. The line between this and करवाया is one of distance: कराना keeps things closer to your own hand, while करवाना puts somebody clearly in between. Honest caveat — many speakers use them interchangeably for everyday things, and करवाना is the commoner of the two in speech. काम is masculine, so the verb is कराया, and the agreement is with the object exactly as it has been since Module 9.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The difference is who did the work, not how the sentence feels.

examples.note: काम is masculine, so कराया.
घर is masculine, so कराया again.
No noun object, so the neutral masculine.

common_error.why_en: The perfective of कराना is कराया, agreeing with masculine काम.

practice.prompt_en: You caused it to happen, without an intermediary in the picture. Pick the form.
practice.question: मैंने काम ___ ।

game.question_en: You had the work done — you caused it, without doing it yourself.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. कराया is the causative; कर लिया says you did it and finished it.

items.gloss_en: I got the work done through someone — the second causative

learn.explanation_en: The second causative puts an intermediary in the picture. मैंने काम करवाया — I got the work done, through somebody. It is the form you want for anything you paid or asked another person to do, and in ordinary speech it is more common than कराया, because most of the time somebody else really is doing it. When you name that person they take से, which is level 18. काम is masculine, so करवाया.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Again a difference of who, not of feel — you arranged it rather than doing it.

examples.note: Somebody else did it.
The commonest way to say this.
बनवाना is the second causative of बनना.

common_error.why_en: काम is masculine, so the verb is masculine.

practice.prompt_en: You had somebody else clean it. Pick the form.
practice.question: मैंने घर साफ़ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: करवाया, because a cleaner did the cleaning.

game.question_en: You paid someone to do the work.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. करवाया is the one with somebody clearly standing in between.

summary.recap_en: करना, कराना, करवाना — do it, have it done, have it done through somebody. All three are transitive, so all three take ने and agree with the object. After fourteen levels of nuance, this is a rule you can simply apply.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the two spelling rules that make the whole set predictable.

levels.title_en: The vowel shortens, and a ल appears

items.pronunciation_notes: The root vowel is long in पीना and short in पिलाना — pii against pi. That difference is the whole rule.
items.gloss_en: drink, make drink, have made to drink

learn.explanation_en: पीना has a long ii, and in the causative it shortens: पिलाना. Two things changed. The vowel went short, which happens in every causative built on a long-vowelled root. And a ल appeared, which happens when the root ends in a vowel — पी- has no consonant to attach the ending to, so ल is inserted to carry it. The same two things happen to खाना, सोना and देना. Once you see the pattern the whole set becomes predictable instead of a list to memorise.

vectorless_equivalent.with_vector: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।
vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Not a vector pair. The base verb has the child drinking; the causative has somebody giving them the milk.

examples.note: The base verb, with ने.

examples.hindi: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।
examples.read_as: maaṁ ne bacche ko duudh pilaayaa.
examples.note: First causative, and the child takes को.

examples.english: He had the servant serve tea.
examples.note: Second causative; चाय is feminine, so पिलवाई.

common_error.wrong: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पीलाया।
common_error.right: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।
common_error.why_en: The long ii shortens to i in the causative. Keeping it long is the commonest spelling slip here.

practice.prompt_en: Mother did the giving herself. Pick the form.
practice.question: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: First causative पिलाया — short vowel, inserted ल.

game.question_en: Mother gave the child milk to drink, with her own hands.
options: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।
माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलवाया।
options_read_as: maaṁ ne bacche ko duudh pilaayaa.
maaṁ ne bacche ko duudh pilvaayaa.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. पिलाया is her own hands; पिलवाया would put somebody else in between.

tts_strings: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।

items.pronunciation_notes: खाना has a long aa; खिलाना has a short i. khaa against khi.

learn.explanation_en: खाना behaves exactly like पीना: the root vowel shortens and a ल appears because the root ends in a vowel. खाना, खिलाना, खिलवाना. खिलाना is the ordinary word for feeding somebody and one of the most used causatives in the language, since feeding people is a large part of what Hindi conversation is about. The one thing to accept rather than derive is that the shortening goes to i and not to a short a — the same happens in सीखना and सिखाना.

vectorless_equivalent.with_vector: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खिलाया।
vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Who is eating changes. In the base verb the child eats; in the causative the mother feeds.

examples.note: The base verb.

examples.hindi: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खिलाया।
examples.read_as: maaṁ ne bacche ko khaanaa khilaayaa.
examples.note: First causative, with को on the child.
Second causative — somebody else did the feeding.

common_error.wrong: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खाया।
common_error.right: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खिलाया।
common_error.why_en: The mother is not the one eating, so the causative is required.

practice.prompt_en: Mother did the feeding herself. Pick the form.
practice.question: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: खिलाया — short vowel, inserted ल, first causative.

options: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खिलवाया।
माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खिलाया।
options_read_as: maaṁ ne bacche ko khaanaa khilvaayaa.
maaṁ ne bacche ko khaanaa khilaayaa.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. खिलाया is her own hands; खिलवाया hands the feeding to somebody else.

tts_strings: माँ ने बच्चे को खाना खिलाया।

items.gloss_en: he fed the child — and where को goes

learn.title_en: The person fed takes को, and cannot control the verb
learn.explanation_en: In a first causative the person you act on takes को: उसने बच्चे को खाना खिलाया. There are two nouns after the subject and only one of them is the grammatical object — खाना — so that is what the verb agrees with. बच्चे is को-marked, and as Module 9 established, a को-marked noun cannot control the verb. So खिलाया is masculine because खाना is, and it would stay खिलाया even if the child were a girl. Swap the food for something feminine and the verb moves: उसने बच्ची को रोटी खिलाई.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The causative adds a feeder; the base verb has only an eater.

examples.note: खाना is the object; बच्चे को cannot control the verb.

examples.english: He fed the little girl roti.
examples.note: रोटी is feminine, so खिलाई. The को-marked child is still irrelevant.

examples.hindi: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।
examples.read_as: maaṁ ne bacche ko duudh pilaayaa.
examples.note: The same shape with पिलाना.

common_error.why_en: रोटी is the bare object and it is feminine, so it controls the verb.

practice.prompt_en: The bare object is रोटी, which is feminine. Complete the verb.
practice.question: उसने बच्ची को रोटी ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: रोटी is feminine singular and it is the only noun eligible to control the verb.

game.question_en: He fed the little girl roti, with his own hands.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. खिलाई is his own hands; खिलवाई would mean he had somebody else feed her.

tts_strings: माँ ने बच्चे को दूध पिलाया।

summary.recap_en: Two spelling rules cover the whole causative set: long root vowels shorten, and roots ending in a vowel take an inserted ल. पीना to पिलाना, खाना to खिलाना. The person acted on takes को and therefore cannot control the verb — the bare object does.
summary.next_up_en: Next: three more ladders, including two verbs you have been using all along without noticing.

learn.explanation_en: पढ़ाना means to teach, and you have been using it since Module 6 without knowing it was a causative. It is one: to teach is to cause somebody to read. The root vowel here is already short, so nothing shortens and the ladder runs straight down — पढ़ना, पढ़ाना, पढ़वाना. The third rung, पढ़वाना, is what you do when you hire a tutor: you have somebody taught rather than teaching them yourself.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The base verb has the children reading; the causative has somebody teaching them.

examples.note: The base verb, agreeing with feminine किताब.
First causative. बच्चों को is को-marked, so the verb stays neutral.
Second causative — a tutor was involved.

common_error.why_en: Teaching requires the causative. पढ़ा would say he read them, which is not the meaning.

practice.prompt_en: He taught them himself. Pick the form.
practice.question: उसने बच्चों को ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पढ़ाया — the first causative, which is simply the word for teach.

game.question_en: You hired a tutor for the children.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. पढ़वाया puts the tutor in between; पढ़ाया would mean you taught them yourself.

items.pronunciation_notes: बनना has a doubled n that must be held: ban-naa. बनाना does not.

learn.title_en: A ladder that starts one rung lower
learn.explanation_en: This one begins with an intransitive verb. बनना means to become, to be made. बनाना is its causative — to make. And बनवाना is the second — to have made. So the word you have been using for "make" since Module 4 is itself a causative, and there is a rung below it you may never have noticed. The ने consequence follows automatically: बनना is intransitive, so घर बना takes no ने, while मैंने घर बनाया does.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The base is intransitive and has no agent at all; the causatives add one, and with it ने.

examples.note: Intransitive, so no ने and no agent.
First causative, transitive, so ने appears.
Second causative — builders did the building.

common_error.why_en: बनना is intransitive and takes no ने. If you want ने you need बनाया.

practice.prompt_en: You had somebody else build it. Pick the form.
practice.question: मैंने घर ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: बनवाया — the second causative, with builders in between.

game.question_en: You hired builders and had the house built.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. बनवाया names you as the one who arranged it; बनाया would say you built it.

items.pronunciation_notes: सीखना has a long ii and सिखाना a short i, with the aspirated kh in both.

learn.explanation_en: सीखना has a long ii and it shortens: सिखाना. The same change as पीना to पिलाना, except that सीखना's root ends in a consonant, so no ल is needed. Between those two verbs you have the entire spelling rule — long vowels shorten, and vowel-final roots take a ल. Worth noting that Hindi now gives you two words for teach. पढ़ाना is teaching a subject; सिखाना is teaching a skill. You पढ़ाना history, and you सिखाना somebody to drive.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Who is doing the learning changes. The base has me learning; the causative has him teaching.

examples.note: हिंदी is feminine, so सीखी.
हिंदी is still the bare object, so सिखाई.
तैरना is an infinitive and therefore masculine, so सिखाया.

common_error.why_en: The long ii shortens in the causative.

practice.prompt_en: He taught you Hindi himself. Pick the form.
practice.question: उसने मुझे हिंदी ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: सिखाई — short vowel, first causative, agreeing with feminine हिंदी.

game.explanation_en: All four are correct. सिखाई is him teaching; सिखवाई would mean he arranged for somebody else to.

summary.recap_en: पढ़ाना and बनाना were causatives all along. बनना adds a rung below बनाना and is intransitive, so it takes no ने. सीखना shortens to सिखाना. And Hindi has two words for teach — पढ़ाना for a subject, सिखाना for a skill.
summary.next_up_en: Next: naming the person who actually did it, and the causative you will use most in real life.

levels.title_en: Naming the agent, and everyday use

items.pronunciation_notes: उससे has a doubled s that must be held: us-se.
items.gloss_en: I got him to do the work — the agent takes से

learn.title_en: The person who actually did it takes से
learn.explanation_en: When you name the intermediary in a second causative, they take से: मैंने उससे काम करवाया — I got the work done by him. Not को, and not ने. That is worth holding on to, because three postpositions are now in play in a single sentence and only one of them is right for the agent. Compare the first causative, where the person you act on takes को: मैंने बच्चे को खिलाया. The rough rule is को for the person acted on, से for the person acting on your behalf.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both describe the same work getting done. One names you as the arranger; the other names him as the doer.

examples.english: I got him to do the work.
examples.note: The agent takes से.
नौकर से, and खाना is what the verb agrees with.

examples.english: He had me write the letter.
examples.note: चिट्ठी is feminine, so लिखवाई.

common_error.why_en: The person doing the work on your behalf takes से, not को.

practice.prompt_en: He is the one who did the work, on your behalf. Pick the postposition.
practice.question: मैंने ___ काम करवाया।
practice.explanation_en: से marks the agent of a causative.

game.question_en: You got him to do the work on your behalf, and you want him named.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. The third is the only one that both names him and keeps you as the arranger.

items.gloss_en: I got my hair cut — the everyday causative

learn.title_en: The form you need at the barber's
learn.explanation_en: This is where causatives stop being grammar and start being useful. Anything done to you as a service goes in the second causative, and the person who did it usually goes unmentioned: मैंने बाल कटवाए, I got my hair cut. बाल is masculine plural, so कटवाए. The same shape covers a great deal of ordinary life — मैंने कपड़े सिलवाए, मैंने गाड़ी ठीक करवाई. Saying मैंने बाल काटे instead would mean you cut your own hair, which is a different afternoon entirely.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both are correct and they describe different events — one at a barber's, one with your own scissors.

examples.note: बाल is masculine plural, so कटवाए.
The base verb — you did it yourself.
गाड़ी is feminine, so करवाई.

common_error.why_en: बाल is masculine plural, so the verb is plural too.

practice.prompt_en: A barber did it, and बाल is masculine plural. Pick the form.
practice.question: मैंने बाल ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: Second causative for a service, and plural to agree with बाल.

game.question_en: You went to a barber and had your hair cut.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi describing different situations. कटवाए is the one with a barber in it.

items.pronunciation_notes: प्रेरणार्थक is the grammatical term; you will not need to say it, only to recognise it in a textbook.

learn.title_en: Three rungs, two spelling rules, two postpositions
learn.explanation_en: The ladder, complete. Rung one is the base verb: करना, खाना, पढ़ना, सीखना. Rung two adds -आ-: कराना, खिलाना, पढ़ाना, सिखाना — you cause it, fairly directly. Rung three adds -वा-: करवाना, खिलवाना, पढ़वाना, सिखवाना — somebody stands in between. Two spelling rules cover the whole set: long root vowels shorten, and roots ending in a vowel take an inserted ल. Two postpositions cover the participants: the person acted on takes को, and the person acting on your behalf takes से. And every causative is transitive, so the perfective takes ने and the verb agrees with the bare object.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: The base verb says you did it. Everything the ladder adds is about who really did, and through whom.

examples.note: Rung one.
Rung two.

examples.english: I got him to do the work.
examples.note: Rung three, with से on the agent.

common_error.why_en: The child is the person acted on, so को. से would make the child the one doing the feeding.

practice.prompt_en: The child is the one being fed. Pick the postposition.
practice.question: मैंने बच्चे ___ खाना खिलाया।
practice.explanation_en: को for the person acted on; से would make them the agent instead.

game.question_en: You got someone else to do the work for you.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. The third names the agent and puts you in the arranging role, which is what the situation calls for.

summary.recap_en: The agent of a causative takes से — मैंने उससे काम करवाया — while the person acted on takes को. Services you have performed on you go in the second causative with the agent unmentioned: मैंने बाल कटवाए. That completes the ladder, and the module.
